Why are European semi-trucks (lorries) so boxy, while American ones look more like a regular truck?
in america the length is determined by the trailer, in europe the cab is included, so it cuts into cargo space.
Here in eastern Canada I see alot of lorries these days. They are slowly replacing the van.

Generally in Europe lorries have to cover shorter distances, while in America most transport routes are longer. At the same time, European cities usually have more narrow roads with tight turns - as many of them weren't laid out with automobiles in mind. This favours shorter and more manoeuvrable designs (better suited for cities) in Europe and bigger and more comfortable designs (better suited for very long routes) designs in the US. If you look at Australian lorries, they're similar to trucks that you see in the US. Australia also has many long routes, and cities with more truck-friendly road layouts.
Hmm good to know, that actually makes a lot of sense
The shorter cab length also makes turning easier. As in most European cities the roads are not that wide and corners are tight.
